domestic.title: LGのデジタルサイネージおよびクラウドソリューションが「ヨシロットン展 彼方との交信／BEYOND EARTH」に採用
domestic.content:
【ニュースの要約】
本展示では、32インチデジタルサイネージ「32UL5Q-M」148台に加え、クラウド型コンテンツ管理ソリューション「LG SuperSign Cloud」およびリモート監視ソリューション「LG ConnectedCare」が採用されています。会場内に設置された140台超のサイネージをクラウド上で一元管理することで、運営スタッフは場所を問わずコンテンツの更新・配信を行えるほか、各ディスプレイの稼働状況をリアルタイムで把握することが可能となります。

当社は近年、デジタルサイネージ製品のみならず、コンテンツ管理や遠隔監視を支えるソリューションのラインナップを進めています。本展示は、大規模なデジタルサイネージ運用を支えるソリューション基盤として、クリエイティブな表現と効率的な運営の両立に貢献する導入事例です。

RGBシリーズ過去最大規模となる、144台のモニターディスプレイを使用したインスタレーション作品を、LG社の協力のもと実現することができました。この作品の原点にあるのは、幼少期にコンピュータールームで目にしたスクリーンセーバーの映像です。画面の中に次々と現れる色や形、動きに衝撃を受けた体験は、その後の自分のグラフィックやビジュアル表現へと興味へとつながっていきました。

今回のインスタレーションでは、その記憶と、家電量販店に無数のモニターディスプレイが並ぶ光景から着想を得ています。これほどの数のモニターディスプレイを同時にコントロールし、ひとつの作品として成立させることは、技術的にも決して容易ではありません。今回、LG社の最新技術によって144台のモニターを連動させることが可能となり、RGBシリーズにおける新しい表現のかたちを実現することができました。

■ LGエレクトロニクス・ジャパン ID Team Team Leader櫻井 佑亮 コメント

このたび、YOSHIROTTEN氏による大規模個展において、当社のデジタルサイネージおよびクラウド型サイネージソリューションを採用いただいたことを大変光栄に思います。本展示では140台超のサイネージを活用した空間演出が行われますが、LGは高品質な表示性能に加え、コンテンツ管理や遠隔監視までを含めたソリューションを提供することで、運営効率の向上と安定した展示環境の実現に寄与することを目指しています。今後もLGは、さまざまな空間で新たな体験価値の創出を支えるパートナーとして、革新的なディスプレイソリューションを提供してまいります。

本製品は、商業施設や店舗で求められる視認性と信頼性を追求した32インチ商業用デジタルサイネージです。500cd/平方メートル の高輝度パネルを採用し、明るい空間でも鮮明な映像表示を実現。また、電源基板には防湿・防塵効果を高めるコンフォーマルコーティングを施しているほか、24時間連続稼働や15°チルト設置にも対応し、さまざまな空間で高い運用性を発揮します。

複数のデジタルサイネージをクラウド上で一元管理できるコンテンツ管理ソリューションです。コンテンツの作成から配信、更新までを単一のプラットフォームで行うことができ、複数台のディスプレイに対する遠隔運用を実現します。テンプレートやスケジュール配信機能も備えており、大規模な展示会や商業施設において効率的かつ柔軟なコンテンツ運用を支援します。

デジタルサイネージの稼働状況を遠隔から監視・管理できるクラウドベースのソリューションです。各ディスプレイの状態や異常をリアルタイムで把握できるため、迅速な対応と安定した運用を支援します。また、管理ダッシュボードによる一元的なモニタリングにより、大規模なサイネージ運用における保守負荷を軽減。展示会や商業施設など、多数のディスプレイを活用する環境で効率的な運営を実現します。

【YOSHIROTTEN（ヨシロットン）氏・プロフィール】

domestic.title: 店内広告は「邪魔」から「役立つ」へ リテールメディア が狙う購入直前の新接点（DIGIDAY［日本版］）

relatedNews.title: 店内広告は「邪魔」から「役立つ」へ リテールメディア が狙う購入直前の新接点

domestic.content:
【ニュースの要約】
同チェーンは店内メディア企業のルーマ（Looma）との提携により、2026年10月から1200店舗で、広告や教育的コンテンツを流すデジタルスクリーンを導入する計画だ。ウォルグリーンズによれば、ルーマを選んだ理由は、訴求する商品のすぐ横にデジタルスクリーンを設置する手法にあるという。

ウォルグリーンズは、これによって「買い物客の邪魔をするのではなく、教育することを目的としたコンテンツを届ける」ことができ、また広告の再生回数だけでなく、フルファネルの指標を使ってパフォーマンスを測定できるとしている。

ルーマは10の小売チェーンで7000台を超えるスクリーンのネットワークを持ち、クローガー（Kroger）、H-E-B、ハリス・ティーター（Harris Teeter）、BJ'sホールセール（BJ's Wholesale）などの小売店で、月間1300万人のユニークな買い物客にリーチしている。

このテック企業は2018年、ガラスの代わりにデジタルスクリーンを備えた冷蔵庫の扉をウォルグリーンズの店舗に設置しはじめた。このスクリーンには、庫内にあるとされる商品の陳列棚が仮想的に表示されるほか、広告も流れる仕組みだった。

しかし、米経済メディアのブルームバーグ（Bloomberg）が2025年に報じたところによると、冷蔵庫のパネルがちらついたり、フリーズしたり、誤った商品を表示したり、さらには発火したりすることもあったという。

同メディアによれば、クーラースクリーンズは2023年、契約から撤退したとしてウォルグリーンズを提訴し、シカゴ地域の100以上の店舗へのデータ配信をひそかに停止した。この訴訟は現在も続いているとみられる。

クーラースクリーンズのディスプレイとは異なり、今回のスクリーンは商品の視界を遮るのではなく、商品の横に設置される。

domestic.title: イオンのリテールメディアの強みは「規模」と「多様さ」 WAON POINT紐づくID-POSデータ活用を本格化・一気通貫の販促支援へ
domestic.source: Agenda note (アジェンダノート)
domestic.content:
【ニュースの要約】
幅広いデータから「経済合理性だけでない顧客解像度も」

イオンマーケティングは9月18日、国内最大級の小売企業グループであるイオングループの店舗網と膨大な顧客データを活用したリテールメディアの取り組みについてメディア向け説明会を行った。

同社は従来から、店舗・顧客データを活用した企業のプロモーション支援に取り組んできた。現在はYouTubeやLINEヤフーといった外部メディアとの連携や、年間アクティブユーザー約5000万人・年間購買4.4兆円にのぼるWAON POINTに紐づくID-POSデータを活用したレジクーポンの配信最適化を本格化させている。さらに来春には、WAON POINTの全量データに加え、インテージグループと連携した購買パネルデータも活用する大規模データプラットフォーム「MIXT Platform」の運用を開始する予定だ。定量分析による仮説立案からターゲティング、販促試作の実行、効果検証までを一気通貫で提供し、企業のマーケティング活動を支援していくと意欲を示した。

グループのリテールメディア事業について概要説明するイオンマーケティング 常務取締役（事業本部統括責任者）の長島弘明氏（右奥）

アプリや店頭サイネージなど小売事業者の持つ巨大な顧客接点をメディア化し、膨大な顧客データに基づき効果的に広告を配信できるリテールメディアは近年、新たな収益の柱として注目度を急激に増している。国内ではファミリーマートが店頭サイネージを活用したリテールメディアを他社に先駆けて強化。今年8月に行われたセブン-イレブン・ジャパンによるメーカー向け発表会には900人超が参加するなど、リテールメディア市場への期待の大きさをうかがわせた。

説明会に登壇したイオンマーケティング 常務取締役（事業本部統括責任者）の長島弘明氏はリテールメディアに関する社内の基盤整備について、「先行している企業にようやく近づいてきた」と、これまでの出遅れを率直に認めた。一方で、国内約4万6000店舗に導入されているWAON POINTに紐づいた膨大なID-POSデータと、リアル店舗における豊富かつさまざまなライフスタイルに寄り添った顧客接点、そしてGMS（総合スーパー）やドラッグストア事業以外にもエンタメなど幅広い事業領域を持つ国内最大級の小売グループならではの「多様さ」が、他社との差別化になり得るとの見方を示した。

「ある意味では、経済的合理性だけでは割り切れないものまで解像度を上げられるのではないか。今後はそういった知見や属性データの規模を組み合わせ、お客さまの解像度を上げて取引先企業を支援することに注力していきたい」（長島氏）

長島氏は10月のリテールアジェンダ2026にも登壇

10月28日-29日に都内で開催されるカンファレンス「 リテールアジェンダ2026」 （ナノベーション主催）でも、リテールが持つ顧客データの活用は重要トピックのひとつに位置づけられている。長島氏はキーノート#2の「進化するトレードマーケティング：『目的地としての店舗』を共創する新たなエコシステム」に登壇予定。リテールが持つ顧客データやAIが導くインサイトを共通言語に、いかにして新たな「来店機会」を創出していくかを議論する。

株式会社インセクト・マイクロエージェンシー  株式会社インセクト・マイクロエージェンシー（所在地：東京都千代田区、代表取締役：赤津 直紀、以下インセクト）は、2026年5月18日（月）に開業したする「東急ステイ メルキュール 広島」（運営：東急リゾーツ＆ステイ株式会社、所在地：広島市中区鉄砲町8-19）のロビーに、タッチ型デジタルサイネージ「FLOWNAVI」を導入します。

ゲストとスタッフの両方が情報を投稿・共有できる参加型のデジタルサイネージです。地元広島を拠点とするイラストレーター・船本トオルさんの手描きマップをベースに、広島ならではのローカル情報を発信します。       ■ 導入背景  「スタッフとゲストの会話が始まるようなマップを作りたい」--そんな東急ステイ メルキュール 広島の想いから、今回の導入が実現しました。観光情報を一方的に届けるのではなく、スタッフの生の声やゲストの旅の記憶が積み重なることで、コンテンツがホテルとともに育っていく--そのような体験を目指して設計しました。

２. 知られざる広島のうわさ話と、少し足を伸ばした旅の提案  「DISCOVER HIROSHIMA」では、地元ならではの"うわさ話"--広島の街や文化に根ざしたエピソード・豆知識を、かわいいイラストとともに紹介します。また「BEYOND Hiroshima」では、呉・尾道など広島市内から少し足を伸ばせるエリアも特集。「次はここへも行ってみよう」というきっかけを届けます。

global.title: The case for and against retail media networks as brand-building channels
global.titleEn: The case for and against retail media networks as brand-building channels
global.content:
【ニュースの要約】
Only a few spots left to join us for AI Marketing Strategies

Join us Sept. 24 in NYC to connect with execs from Digitas, Claire's, Marriott, Havas and others

By  Kimeko McCoy    •   September 21, 2026   •

The original pitch of retail media networks was to find shoppers while they’re shopping and make the sale. Now that RMNs have accomplished that, they’re trying to convince advertisers (and more of their wallets) that they can build their brands on their respective channels.

The capabilities are there. For every retailer that isn’t Amazon — the woolly mammoth of retail media with its own tech stack, measurement capabilities and streaming channel — RMNs have juiced this offering with partnerships. Meaning, retailers that don’t have their own streaming platforms or tech stacks, they’ve inked partnerships to roll out those offerings. For example, Kroger’s partnership with Disney Advertising, Walmart’s partnerships with TikTok, Meta and Snap or Instacart’s partnerships with NBCUniversal.

“Retailers own far more than online ad placements. They own aisles, screens, apps, content and cultural moments,” Kim Mayo, executive director of retail media at Trade School told Digiday in an emailed statement.

For example, in Q4 of 2025, 60% of Walmart’s self-serve display spend went to offsite inventory,  according to a recent Tinuiti report.

But brands still need convincing. Execs say that comes down to part education from the agency and part budgeting from the brand. Some marketers are hooked on ROAS, putting brand growth in the backseat. And for some brands that are focused on brand growth, the right person might not be in the room to pitch as  there’s a tug of war  over who controls retail media budgets.

“You can have all the capabilities in the world, if advertisers can’t agree how to fund it, then you’re never in the running,” said one retail media expert who spoke on the condition of anonymity. They added that the majority of dollars are still being spent with RMNs as conversions.

Retailers control physical aisles, digital screens, apps, and cultural moments where shoppers already are. In theory, retailers could offer brands storytelling opportunities in those spaces and serve up what they’re good at: closed loop measurement.

global.titleEn: SOLUM to Showcase ESL, E-Paper Signage, Digital Signage and Retail Innovation Solutions at Groceryshop 2026
global.content:
【ニュースの要約】
LAS VEGAS ,  Sept. 22, 2026  /PRNewswire/ -- SOLUM, a global provider of Electronic Shelf Labels (ESL), E-Paper Signage (EPS) and retail digital solutions, today announced its participation in Groceryshop 2026, taking place September 22-24 at Mandalay Bay in Las Vegas.  Groceryshop brings together leading grocery, mass retail, convenience, pharmacy, consumer packaged goods (CPG) and retail technology companies to explore the latest trends and innovations shaping the future of commerce.

Featured solutions include:

Electronic Shelf Labels (ESL)

Smart Store Operations Solutions

Retail IoT-Based Store Management Solutions

Drawing on extensive experience serving leading retailers worldwide, SOLUM delivers technologies that help optimize pricing and promotional execution, streamline store operations, and improve overall operational efficiency.  "Digital transformation is becoming increasingly important as retailers seek to improve operational efficiency while enhancing customer experiences," said Tim McCracken, Chief Revenue Officer of SOLUM America. "At Groceryshop 2026, we look forward to engaging with retailers and industry partners and demonstrating solutions that support smarter and more efficient store operations."  Throughout the event, SOLUM will provide live demonstrations and business consultations for visitors at Booth #1409.   About SOLUM   SOLUM is a global technology company specializing in Electronic Shelf Labels (ESL), E-Paper Signage (EPS), digital signage, IoT solutions, and power electronics technologies. The company provides ESL and store digitalization solutions to leading retailers worldwide, helping customers enhance operational efficiency, improve customer engagement, and enable data-driven store operations. Through its global network, SOLUM continues to drive innovation across retail, industrial, and power solutions.  SOURCE SOLUM

global.title: Why VXT is the best digital signage software for small businesses
global.titleEn: Why VXT is the best digital signage software for small businesses
global.content:
【ニュースの要約】
If you own a small business, you know how much work it takes to attract customers, build your brand, boost revenue and stay ahead of the competition. The best digital signage software and content management system (CMS) can make achieving those goals easier.

Older digital signage systems often complicate the process and add hassle, as they require someone to walk a flash drive from screen to screen or wire a computer to every display. With the enhanced  Samsung VXT,  all that comes to an end. Combined with digital signage, the remotely managed VXT is able to generate attention-grabbing content and engaging in-store experiences to improve your bottom line. Here’s how.

A brand-building user experience that boosts revenue

Samsung VXT, a cloud-based CMS, allows you to tailor displays to business needs across multiple industries, including retail, hospitality, sports, finance and food and beverage.

Restaurant owners highlight deals and tempt diners

Elevate your restaurant with a dynamic digital menu or order-confirmation board. Use a  digital menu display  to showcase daily specials, new dishes and bestsellers, as diners buy what they notice. VXT features like Favorites-Based Browsing make it easy to find and reuse your most effective content, while the Content Preview tool ensures your changes appear exactly as expected before going live. You can also eliminate manual data entry and make updates even more quickly by pairing your point-of-sale (POS) system with the Link My POS app, keeping seasonal items, meal combos and limited-time deals current with less work.

Enterprises brand their business and assist shoppers

Samsung retail LED digital signage  serves as a silent salesperson. Sleek, easily updated displays make for a unique in-store experience, helping customers find what they’ve come to buy and promoting on-sale items, new arrivals and seasonal deals. The Info Card feature provides customers with quick-access details on products, services and promotions, while the Weather Channel widget keeps your signage relevant with real-time updates. Enhanced ticker customization also lets you time promotional messages to specific events, so your signage adapts automatically as conditions change.

Boutique owners showcase merchandise

VXT enables business owners to elevate visual merchandising and create engaging in-store experiences that prompt buyers to take action. Many purchases are impulsive, and digital signage helps convert those impulses into revenue. With Global Tags and Essential Tags, you can organize and categorize content efficiently, ensuring you display the right messaging at the right time for maximum impact. Weighted and shuffle playback settings make it easy to give featured merchandise more airtime without rebuilding your playlist from scratch.

The installations are centered around the main entrance to the  casino . First are six column wraps with DSS Architectural solutions. These flexible panels have a 1.8mm pixel pitch and measure 24 feet wide by a towering 14.5 feet high. The six columns can display messaging in concert with each other, separately, or in any combination, creating an entertaining effect for  casino  guests.

Guests can also turn their eyes skyward, where a ceiling display using JCM's DSS Video Wall stretches nearly 12 feet wide and 51 feet long. With a pixel pitch of 1.9mm, the property can curate different atmospheres using crystal-clear video and images, and an easy-to-use controller empowers the property to set the perfect scene for every minute of the day.

Last, in the  casino 's Million Dollar Alley, JCM installed a massive video wall of more than 21 feet wide by 3.5 feet high over a bank of slot machines. The video wall creates a visual destination on the floor and allows the  casino  to highlight new games, promotions, and more.

This project is another in a series of enhancements that JCM is performing at the property over the next year. Previously, JCM installed two landmark Digital Signage Solutions, in the hotel lobby and in the electronic table games area.

Recently, JCM installed CountR's innovative TITA™ Table Game System on each of the  casino 's 325 new table games.

global.title: Horizon Commerce and Pacvue Expand Strategic Partnership to Connect Retail Media Planning, Activation and Measurement
global.titleEn: Horizon Commerce and Pacvue Expand Strategic Partnership to Connect Retail Media Planning, Activation and Measurement
global.content:
【ニュースの要約】
The partnership addresses a persistent challenge for marketers: the systems used to measure media performance and determine investment strategy are often disconnected from the platforms used by teams to execute campaigns. As a result, marketers can identify an opportunity through measurement but are forced to rely on manual processes, separate taxonomies and retailer-specific metrics to translate that insight into action.

Blu Commerce and Pacvue's technology works in lockstep, feeding performance back into the next cycle of planning and optimization. Pacvue's real-time commerce signals – including availability, pricing, and content health – keep activation aligned with what's happening on the digital shelf. The result is a common decision framework connecting senior marketing leadership and campaign practitioners, helping brands allocate investment more effectively, reduce inefficient spend and drive greater incremental sales.

Pacvue is the leading Commerce Media OS, powering over $12B in advertising spend across 100+ global retail media networks including Amazon, Walmart, Target, Kroger, Instacart, Criteo, and CitrusAd. Powered by industry-leading AI and real-time data, Pacvue enables over 70,000 brands and agencies to maximize advertising performance, drive incrementality, and expand reach across the commerce universe from a single mission control. As of 2025, Pacvue powers 12% of total retail media ad spend worldwide excluding China. Combined with Helium 10's SMB solutions, Pacvue delivers the industry's most comprehensive platform for businesses of all sizes. Founded in 2018, Pacvue spans Seattle, Los Angeles, Chicago, New York, Washington D.C., London, Shanghai, and Tokyo. Discover more at pacvue.com.

global.title: Big-Box Briefing: Best Buy puts CTV at the center of its retail media pitch
global.titleEn: Big-Box Briefing: Best Buy puts CTV at the center of its retail media pitch
global.content:
【ニュースの要約】
Best Buy is increasingly putting its electronics roots at the heart of its retail media pitch.

On Wednesday, Best Buy held its annual showcase event highlighting what’s coming up in its retail media business — including a new part of its advertising business that the company is branding as Best Buy CTV.

According to a spokesperson, Best Buy CTV is “a new offering that combines Best Buy’s first-party shopper audiences, device ownership data and purchase-intent signals with premium CTV inventory from partners,” including LG, Roku and Amazon.

For example, advertisers will now have access to advertising inventory on all new and existing Insignia TVs — the name for Best Buy’s in-house TV brand, which uses Amazon’s Fire TV as the operating system.

At the event, Best Buy also announced it is launching on TikTok Shop in late October and expanding its Best Buy Creator program. All of these announcements ladder up to one of the big goals in Best Buy’s retail media business right now, according to Best Buy’s Chief Ads and Media Officer, Lisa Valentino — that is, “finding really unique ways to aggregate supply” for its advertisers.

With Best Buy CTV, in particular, “that is a really unique solution that gets marketers thinking about Best Buy differently” — specifically, that it is an advertising business focused on more than just lower-funnel advertising placements and “can solve problems across all of [your] media.”

Valentino joined Best Buy in 2024 and, before that, spent more than five years at the Walt Disney Company. Now, she’s responsible for shaping the vision for Best Buy’s advertising business under incoming CEO Jason Bonfig, who will take over the top job at the end of October.

“One of the priorities Jason has set forth for us as an enterprise is really about how we advance Best Buy as a retail media and advertising and technology company,” Valentino said. As she put it, areas like CTV and social commerce are now capabilities required to “be an excellent media company and to fuel a large-sized business.”

Of course, adding more supply also gives retailers like Best Buy more places to sell ads and, thus, increase the money they can make through their retail media businesses. Last year, at the same advertising showcase event, Best Buy announced an  in-store takeover package  that advertisers could participate in.  “There is no shortage of ways that retail media networks can add supply,” said Andrew Lipsman, an independent analyst with Media, Ads + Commerce. “They can make more ad slots available in their owned media environments, on-site and in-store. And then there’s a virtually limitless supply that can be obtained via third-party media partnerships and programmatic.”  But what is often lacking, Lipsman said, is quality inventory. CTV, he said, is high-quality inventory, especially when paired with first-party shopper data — which Best Buy can offer.

As part of the Fire TV deal, Best Buy Ads will start using Amazon Ads’ programmatic technology, beginning in February 2027.

Target Corporation declared a quarterly dividend of $1.16 per share, payable on December 1, 2026, and rolled out new premium beauty, food, and home-care partnerships across hundreds of stores and Target.com.   Growth in Target's higher-margin Roundel retail media business and the curated Beauty Studio concept reflects a tilt toward more service-driven revenue streams.   The focus now is on how this mix of retail media and premium partnerships could influence Target's broader investment narrative.     Compare Target’s mix of premium partnerships, retail media and regular dividends with other retailers by reviewing a curated set of resilient balance sheet plays in our  list of solid balance sheet and fundamentals (23 results)     Advertisement       Target Investment Narrative Recap   To own Target, you need to believe the retailer can keep pushing shoppers toward higher margin areas like Roundel, Beauty Studio and premium food while holding onto share in everyday essentials. In the near term, the key issue remains execution on omnichannel convenience and merchandising that actually resonates with younger households, not just adding more product on shelves.   The latest dividend affirmation and partnership rollout does not materially change that near term catalyst. The biggest operational risk still lies in cost pressure and execution gaps in e-commerce versus top competitors, where missteps could erode margins and limit the benefit of these newer, higher margin revenue streams.   The dividend announcement is a clear marker of where Target is today. Management is choosing to maintain a long dividend track record with a US$1.16 quarterly payout and a history that now stretches to a 237th consecutive distribution since 1967, while still investing heavily in media, store experience and technology.   For you as an investor, that mix of ongoing cash returns and spending on Roundel, Beauty Studio and supply chain upgrades defines the trade off. The payout supports a more income oriented thesis, but the key factor still lies in how quickly these newer businesses scale relative to rising labor, regulatory and online fulfillment costs.   Target Earnings and Revenue Assumptions   Target's narrative projects US$119.0b revenue and US$4.6b earnings by 2029. This implies 3.4% yearly revenue growth and an earnings increase of about US$0.2b from US$4.4b today. global.title: AI, value and retail media take center stage at Groceryshop 2026
global.titleEn: AI, value and retail media take center stage at Groceryshop 2026
global.content:
【ニュースの要約】
LAS VEGAS – Groceryshop 2026 wrapped up Thursday at Mandalay Bay after three days of packed sessions, executive discussions and deal-making that underscored just how quickly the grocery industry is changing.  The show drew more than 4,000 executives from across grocery, convenience, pharmacy, dollar and club retail, along with brands, technology vendors and startups. More than 30,000 business meetings were facilitated through Groceryshop's Meetup program, reflecting the event's growing role as a hub for industry networking and partnership building.     While previous editions of Groceryshop have explored emerging technologies and shifting consumer behaviors, this year's event felt different. Rather than discussing future possibilities, retailers and brands came to Las Vegas focused on how to adapt to changes already underway.  Across keynote presentations, panel discussions and hallway conversations, three themes consistently surfaced: the rise of AI-powered shopping, the evolution of value in an era of economic pressure and GLP-1 adoption, and the continued maturation of retail media networks.  Together, those trends are reshaping how consumers discover products, make purchasing decisions and interact with retailers.  Rocquan Lucas, VP of Content at Groceryshop, said: "What we heard at Groceryshop 2026 is that the average grocery shopping cart is about to change more in the next few years than it has in decades as shoppers lean on Al assistants to support their meal planning and cart building, become more selective with their purchases, and in the rise of GLP-1 adoption, shift what and how much they consume.  "That puts real pressure on grocers and brands to make their product data machine readable and deliver the right product and assortment for an evolving consumer, " he added.  AI Moves to the Center of the Shopping Journey  The most dominant topic at Groceryshop was artificial intelligence, and not simply as a back-office tool.  Industry leaders increasingly see AI becoming the first touchpoint in the consumer shopping journey, influencing what products shoppers see, what they buy and even how they build their baskets.  Instacart CEO Chris Rogers set the tone during the opening keynote, arguing that AI could represent the most transformative technology shift grocery has ever experienced.  Rather than manually building shopping lists item by item, Rogers described a future where consumers simply tell an AI assistant what they want. A shopper might request a week's worth of healthy family meals under a specific budget, and an AI agent would instantly generate a personalized cart based on preferences, pricing and product availability.  That vision was echoed by DoorDash co-founder Andy Fang, who positioned AI as a tool for reducing friction rather than replacing consumer choice. The goal, he said, is to help shoppers navigate an increasingly complex marketplace by understanding dietary restrictions, household needs and preferred brands.  Importantly, both executives backed their claims with early performance metrics. According to DoorDash, shoppers using its Ask DoorDash AI assistant are spending more, checking out faster and exploring a wider selection of products than traditional users.  The message for retailers was clear: AI is rapidly becoming a new gateway to commerce.     Retailers are also moving aggressively. Kroger detailed its AI initiatives, which include meal-planning tools tailored to budgets and dietary needs.  Kroger's  Chief Digital Officer,  Yael Cosset  outlined Kroger's Al strategy, from an Al Shopping Assistant that plans meals around budget and dietary needs to Al training for more than 400,000 associates. Dutch grocer Albert Heijn's in-app Al chef, Steijn, now has 1.1 million active users, who spend 56% more than non-users.  "The grocery winners in the age of Al will be the retailer who can earn our trust, your trust, all of our trust in satisfvinq the familv dinner," Cosset said.     Kroger highlights AI strategy rooted in retail expertise at GroceryShop 2026  Yael Cosset, executive vice president and Chief Digital Officer, described a strategy built on using AI to improve the customer experience, make work easier for associates and produce better business outcomes.    Mass Market Retailers  Bill Schiffner         Several speakers emphasized that technology alone will not create competitive advantage. Success depends on the quality of underlying product information and customer data.     Fang delivered perhaps the most practical takeaway of the conference when he noted that nearly all customers prefer products with complete descriptions over those lacking sufficient information. In an AI-driven environment, product data becomes even more important because algorithms can only recommend and explain items based on the information available to them.  Research presented at the event reinforced that point. While enthusiasm for AI is widespread, only a small percentage of enterprises have successfully scaled AI initiatives across their organizations.  That reality produced one of the conference's most memorable insights: before retailers can fully embrace AI, they must first get their data foundations in order.  Value Is Being Redefined  The second major theme focused on consumers and the changing definition of value.  Retail executives and industry analysts repeatedly stressed that today's shopper is far more selective than the consumer of just a few years ago.  Economic pressures continue to influence purchasing decisions, even as inflation has eased from peak levels. According to NielsenIQ, one-third of U.S. households now qualify as financially stretched, a figure that has increased significantly since 2022.  As a result, consumers are not merely searching for discounts. They are strategically assembling baskets that maximize value across price, convenience, nutrition and overall household needs.  Nicole Kalita of NielsenIQ summed up the trend succinctly when she noted that consumers are no longer hunting for deals but assembling them.  At the same time, another force is reshaping food consumption patterns: the continued expansion of GLP-1 medications.  Multiple speakers highlighted growing demand for protein-rich products, healthier options and foods with cleaner ingredient labels as consumers using weight-management drugs rethink eating habits.     Talia Monroe of Chobani argued that consumers are spending more money on fewer calories and reducing purchases of highly processed foods. Unilever Wellbeing CEO Jostein Solheim similarly described GLP-1 adoption as one of the most significant health-related shifts affecting food purchasing behavior.  The discussion generated substantial interest among retailers and manufacturers seeking to understand how changing appetites will influence assortment planning.  One retailer receiving considerable attention was Sam's Club. Chief Merchant Myron Frazier emphasized that value extends beyond product pricing. The company is applying value-focused thinking to services such as delivery, checkout and meal solutions while maintaining consistent pricing across digital and physical channels.  That broader interpretation of value resonated with attendees because it reflects how consumers increasingly evaluate retailers. Convenience, speed and service quality are becoming just as important as price.  Retail Media Continues to Evolve  The third major theme was retail media, which has shifted from an emerging opportunity to a core component of retailer growth strategies.  Industry analyst Andrew Lipsman argued that physical stores remain significantly under-monetized advertising environments. Shoppers spend meaningful time inside stores, yet brands dedicate only a small portion of media budgets to in-store channels.  Examples shared during the conference suggest that is beginning to change.  CVS Media Exchange highlighted several successful in-store initiatives involving digital screens and point-of-sale advertising. Those efforts demonstrated how retailers can leverage existing store traffic to attract advertising dollars while influencing purchase decisions closer to the point of sale.  Despite ongoing momentum, measurement remains a significant challenge.  Research previewed by EMARKETER and Bain revealed that many retail media executives still lack confidence in determining whether revenue is truly incremental. Brands share similar concerns, with relatively few saying they can accurately measure return on investment.  The rise of AI is simultaneously creating new opportunities and new uncertainties.  Some executives worry AI could fundamentally alter how advertising inventory is purchased and optimized. Others view AI as the next major growth engine for retail media, enabling improved targeting, creative formats and measurement capabilities.  Most networks appear to be betting on the latter. Many are already testing AI-powered advertising solutions and exploring new monetization strategies.  The strongest message came from Procter & Gamble's Jacques Hagopian, who argued that retail media works best when integrated into broader business planning. Media, merchandising, inventory management and supply chain coordination must work together to drive sales growth.  That perspective reflects how retail media has matured. It is no longer viewed solely as an advertising product but as part of a larger commercial strategy.  Key Announcements and Final Takeaways  The conference also generated several notable announcements.  Instacart revealed a partnership with Gopuff that will bring Gopuff onto the Instacart Marketplace while expanding access to Instacart's Carrot Ads platform. DoorDash unveiled Brand Center, a new platform designed to provide brands with deeper insights into performance across digital and physical commerce channels. Kroger further outlined its long-term vision for AI-enabled grocery experiences, while California Pizza Kitchen announced plans for a frozen appetizer line developed with Golden West Food Group.  As Groceryshop 2026 concluded, the industry's direction appeared increasingly clear.  AI is rapidly becoming the front door to grocery shopping. Consumers are redefining value around health, convenience and affordability. And retail media is evolving into a strategic business capability rather than simply an advertising channel.  For retailers and brands, the challenge now is execution. The ideas discussed in Las Vegas are no longer distant possibilities. They are becoming competitive necessities.  If Groceryshop 2026 revealed anything, it is that the next grocery revolution will not happen in stores alone. It will occur at the intersection of data, technology and changing consumer expectations. And judging from the conversations at Mandalay Bay this week, that transformation is already well underway.

global.title: Groceryshop Outlook: GLP-1s, Retail Media, AI Top List
global.titleEn: Groceryshop Outlook: GLP-1s, Retail Media, AI Top List
global.content:
【ニュースの要約】
Planning for GLP-1s and cost-conscious shoppers

Witcher urged grocers and brands to plan for a greater GLP-1 impact. According to a June 2026 study by PwC, GLP-1 adoption has more than doubled in 16 months. Users now live in 21 percent of U.S. households, up from 9 percent, and 54 percent have been taking the drugs for more than a year.

Yet the Shoptalk 2026 Grocery Pulse Survey found 17 percent of grocery executives expect GLP-1s to cut top-line sales by 5-10 percent during the next five years, and just 2 percent expect a bigger hit. With 72 percent of U.S. adults overweight and 40.2 percent classed as obese, Witcher warned that the impact could be far greater than the industry expects.

“Brands are already starting to market to GLP-1 users on their packaging, and Walmart is advertising in its stores that it’s the source for ‘all your GLP-1 needs,'” said Witcher. “Retailers with pharmacy services, like Walmart, Albertsons and CVS, may have an advantage.”

Witcher also challenged grocers and brands to plan for cost-conscious shoppers. Eighty percent of Americans are trying to cut spending, and 28 percent are cutting back on groceries, according to Bain & Company. Of those, 49 percent are buying fewer items, 56 percent are trading down to cheaper brands and 44 percent are leaning harder on discounts.

According to the Shoptalk survey, 58 percent of brand executives expect placement on grocers’ websites, apps and in-store displays to matter much more in the next one to five years.

Preparing store teams for AI

On AI, grocery leaders are more positive than most Americans. Sixty-four percent of Americans worry AI will displace jobs, according to Anthropic. But the Shoptalk survey found 85 percent of grocery executives expect store associates to become customer advisors, product specialists or experience managers as AI removes or reduces their tasks. Ninety-two percent say AI-enabled mobile devices for associates are important, rising to 97 percent among grocers.

“Employees will evolve into shopper experience specialists,” said Witcher. “That means grocers and brands will need to rethink, reprioritize and retrain for how employees interact with shoppers, helping them find and compare products, understand ingredients and discover new products they haven’t tried before. Shoppers already use their phones to look up product information and reviews and to load coupons. Associates should have those same tools if grocers want to meet shoppers’ expectations for service.”

The Shoptalk Grocery Pulse Survey was fielded July 29–Aug. 5 among 88 respondents at the director level and above: 39 from grocery retailers and 49 from brands.

global.title: nsign and Sony simplify digital signage deployment
global.titleEn: nsign and Sony simplify digital signage deployment
global.content:
【ニュースの要約】
“When you are deploying signage across multiple locations, every extra device and every configuration step adds up,” said Mónica Fernández, managing director of nsign. “Working with Sony gives our partners a simpler way to get screens up and running and keep them under control. It also gives customers more choice as their networks grow, while keeping content and day-to-day operations in one familiar platform.”

To simplify deployment, installers use a predefined provisioning profile through Sony’s Device Provisioning Tool. The profile installs nsign as the display’s default application and applies the settings required for remote monitoring and control. Once activated and paired with the nsign platform, the display launches the application automatically at startup. This reduces repetitive manual configuration and helps integrators apply a consistent setup across multiple screens and locations.

Through Sony’s local REST API, the nsign application can control supported displays, including switching screens on and off, rebooting them and changing screen orientation. Content, playlists and schedules are managed centrally through nsign, bringing playback and display control into the same operational environment.

The collaboration also expands the hardware options available to nsign customers. Supported BRAVIA Professional Displays can be managed alongside other compatible devices, including Android-based hardware and BrightSign players. A retailer or restaurant chain can introduce Sony screens at new locations or in a pilot project while retaining its existing compatible hardware elsewhere. Marketing and operations teams continue to use the same platform to manage content across the network, without having to adopt a separate workflow for each hardware manufacturer.

Return on advertising spend is a useful performance metric, but only with accurate attribution.

ROAS connects advertising investment to revenue. The calculation is simple:

ROAS = (Sales Attributed to Ads) / (Cost of Ads)

The  result  can help marketers compare campaigns and allocate budgets.

ROAS’s usefulness depends on the accuracy of its attribution.

domestic.title: サイバーエージェントの最新事例に学ぶ「リテールメディアで効くAIクリエイティブ」オンライン勉強会を開催【10/20 参加者募集中】
domestic.source: Agenda note (アジェンダノート)
domestic.content:
【ニュースの要約】
購買の瞬間、生活者に響くクリエイティブをどう生み出す？

マーケティング専門メディア「アジェンダノート（運営：ナノベーション）」が2023年12月に設立した、リテールメディアおよびリテールデータを活用したマーケティングの研究組織「リテールデータマーケティングコンソーシアム」。

同コンソーシアムが主催する定期勉強会（ウェビナー）が、10月20日（火）18:00-19:00に開催される。

今回のテーマは 「AIクリエイティブの現在と未来 ―リテールメディアにおけるクリエイティブを考える― 」 。

⽣成AIの進化によって、広告クリエイティブのあり方は大きく変わろうとしている。ひとつの表現を「つくる」ことから、多様なクリエイティブを生み出し、検証を重ねながら、より効果の高い表現へと磨き込んでいく時代へと移りつつある。

⼀⽅、店頭サイネージやアプリ、ECなどのリテールメディアでは、購買の直前、あるいはまさに購買しようとしている⽣活者と接する。そのため、マス広告やWeb広告とは異なる発想でのクリエイティブ設計が求められる。

本ウェビナーでは、AIクリエイティブをめぐる最新動向や実践事例を紹介しながら、「売り場の⽂脈」「購買データ」「ブランドらしさ」をいかに掛け合わせ、購買の瞬間に生活者の心を動かす表現へとつなげていくのかを考える。

さらに、AIによる表現の自動化が進むなかで、人だからこそ担える役割とは何か。クリエイティブにおける「人とAIの役割分担」のこれからについても展望する。

毛利氏は2017年にAI クリエイティブ部門を立ち上げ、AIや3DCG を活用した広告クリエイティブの効果予測や自動生成に関する研究開発において、ビジネス開発責任者・統括として事業を推進してきた。

一方、藤田氏は2020年、小売のDXを推進するDX本部の統括に就任。サツドラ・AWLとの業務提携をはじめ、国内のチェーンストア各社との連携を通じて、小売領域におけるDXを推進してきた。

domestic.title: セイビ堂「Unicorn Media DOOH for BrightSign」にデジタルサイネージプレーヤー『BrightSign』が採用
domestic.content:
【ニュースの要約】
ジャパンマテリアル株式会社（代表取締役社長執行役員：田中宏典、三重県三重郡、以下「当社」）は、株式会社セイビ堂（以下「セイビ堂」）が提供するDOOH（デジタル屋外広告 ） 向け統合パッケージ「Unicorn Media DOOH for BrightSign」に、当社が販売する米国BrightSign社製デジタルサイネージプレーヤー『BrightSign』が採用されたことをお知らせいたします。

評価された『BrightSign』の高い安定性と拡張性

セイビ堂の「Unicorn Media DOOH for BrightSign」は、コンテンツ配信、複数拠点の管理、広告運用、データ活用を一元化するDOOH向け配信・運用システムです。このたび、同システムのサイネージプレーヤーとして当社の『BrightSign』が採用されました。

当システムは、セイビ堂が提供する クラウド型CMS「Unicorn Studio」 と 専用再生アプリケーション「Unicorn Player」 により、複数の大型LEDやデジタルサイネージディスプレイの表示を遠隔から一括管理できます。また、同社の 広告配信プラットフォーム「ROBOTICS AD PLATFORM」 と連携することで、広告枠の管理や配信が可能となり、既存のデジタルサイネージを媒体として活用した収益化をサポートします。さらに、サイネージ周辺の通行量や滞在時間、来訪傾向などを調査・分析する 人流データ活用ソリューション により、広告配信や販促施策の最適化につなげることもできます。

時間や場所に応じた配信予約が可能です。タイムサーバによる時刻同期により、広告運用や厳密な時間管理が求められる場面でも、「時間ぴったり」の配信を実現します。時報コンテンツなども配信可能です。

直感的に操作できる管理画面「Unicorn Studio」を採用しています。毎日のコンテンツ更新や配信設定の負担を大幅に削減します

外部ハードウェアを追加することなく、DSP（Demand Side Platform：広告配信プラットフォーム）と接続可能。空き枠の広告収益化もサポートします。

安定性に定評のあるハードウェアの信頼性に加え、人感センサーをはじめとする各種センサーをトリガーとした高度なインタラクティブ演出などの拡張性もそのままご活用いただけます。

今後のアップデートにより、セイビ堂の監視カメラ連携ソリューション「LiveEye」との接続に対応予定です。設置場所の放映状況をモニタリングすることが可能になります。

サイネージ専用に開発されたSTBです。長期間の使用に耐える安定性にご定評いただいています。

domestic.title: “出社シーンの働く時間”に認知・想起・購買の循環をつくる「オフィス内リテールメディア」を提供開始
domestic.content:
【ニュースの要約】
株式会社Prediction（本社：東京都新宿区、代表取締役社長：大木健一朗、以下Prediction）は、“オフィスで働く時間”で認知・想起・購買の循環をつくる「オフィス内リテールメディア」の提供を開始しました。

本サービスは、全国2,100面・想定リーチ260万人（*1）のビジネスパーソンに接触するオフィス内広告を起点に、広告出稿、オフィス内コンビニへの商品配荷、販売POS分析、ブランドリフト調査までを一気通貫で提供します。

これまで分断されていた「広告で知る」「仕事中に思い出す」「その場で買う」「効果を検証する」という体験を、ビジネスパーソンが長い時間を過ごすオフィスという一つの空間でつなぎます。新商品の販売実績づくりから、定番商品の新たな消費シーン創出まで、ブランド指標と実際の購買行動の双方を可視化できる新たなリテールメディアを目指します。

（*1）想定リーチは4週間放映時。当社媒体ネットワークの設置企業・勤務者数等を基に算出。

サービスサイトURL： https://prediction.co.jp/service/retail-ad/

■6,000億円を超える国内リテールメディア市場。「販促」から「広告」へ広がる投資

国内では、購買データを広告・マーケティングに活用する「リテールメディア」の市場が急速に拡大しています。CARTA HOLDINGSとデジタルインファクトの調査によると、2025年の国内リテールメディア広告市場は6,066億円に達し、2029年には1兆3,174億円まで拡大する見通しです。このうち店舗事業者によるリテールメディア広告市場も、2025年の830億円から2029年には1,939億円まで成長すると予測されています。（*2）

また同調査では、広告主による投資が従来の営業部門による販促費にとどまらず、広告宣伝・マーケティング部門の広告宣伝費にも広がっている一方、ターゲティングや広告効果測定手法の整備が課題として挙げられています。

Predictionは、この市場拡大の中で、ECや店頭に加えて、ビジネスパーソンが日常的に滞在する「オフィス」もまた、広告接触と購買をつなげる新たなリテールメディアになり得ると考えています。

(*2)株式会社CARTA HOLDINGSおよび株式会社デジタルインファクト調べ（ https://cartaholdings.co.jp/news/20260127_1/ ）

1） イオンリテール株式会社 「イオンチャンネルAD」、「イオンチャンネル®」

2） ウエルシア薬局株式会社 「ウエルシア薬局サイネージ」※情報提供元：株式会社MADS

特に店頭デジタルサイネージやアプリ等のリテールメディアは、単なる購買動線上の販促ツールにとどまらず、生活動線上で機能する「新たな認知獲得・ブランド構築のメディア」として急速に重要性を増しています。持続的なブランド成長に向けては、リテールメディアをテレビ広告やデジタル広告などの既存メディアとシームレスに連動させ、相乗効果を最大化する「統合メディアプラニング」の確立が不可欠となります。

こうした状況を受け博報堂と博報堂テクノロジーズは、国内の主要リテールメディア提供企業7社との大規模な連携を実現しました。単一のリテールメディア提供企業にとどまらず、各社が保有する膨大かつ多様なメディアデータを個人情報に配慮した適切な形で集約・分析することで、特定の小売りチャネルに偏ることなく、生活者の幅広い購買行動を捉える独自のシミュレーションロジックを開発しました。

domestic.title: 名古屋駅のデジタルサイネージで防災気象情報を発信 ～新しい防災気象情報のショート動画と天気予報を日英2言語で放映～
domestic.content:
【ニュースの要約】
一般財団法人 日本気象協会（本社：東京都豊島区、理事長：守屋　岳、以下「日本気象協会」）は、2026年10月、名古屋駅構内のデジタルサイネージにて、新しい防災気象情報に関するショート動画および「天気予報」コンテンツを放映します。

本取り組みは、多くの利用者が行き交う名古屋駅にて、気象災害への備えや新しい防災気象情報への理解を深めていただくことを目的として実施するものです。新しい防災気象情報は気象庁が河川氾濫、大雨、土砂災害、高潮を5段階の警戒レベルにあわせて発表するもので、2026年5月29日から運用を開始しています。ショート動画では、新しい防災気象情報のレベル3と4に応じた避難行動について15秒でわかりやすく紹介します。また天気予報では、名古屋市・豊田市・豊橋市を対象に、日本気象協会の3時間ごとのポイント予報を提供し、最新の気象情報をお知らせします。

なお名古屋駅は、国内外から多くの人が利用する交通拠点であることから、ショート動画および天気予報には日本語と英語を併記します。訪日外国人を含む幅広い利用者に向けて、気象情報や防災情報をわかりやすく伝え、防災意識の向上につなげます。

日本気象協会は、今後も気象・防災情報の普及広報を通じて、誰もが必要な情報を適切なタイミングで得られる、安全・安心な社会の実現に貢献していきます。

domestic.title: トライアル×スギ薬局／「東京リテールメディア研究会」設立、共通指標策定へ
domestic.content:
【ニュースの要約】
トライアルホールディングス とスギ薬局は9月30日、小売企業横断のリテールメディアネットワークの構築、効果検証方法の確立、共通指標の策定を研究する「TOKYO Retail Media Federation（東京リテールメディア研究会）」を発足したと発表した。

トライアルホールディングスとスギホールディングスが、1月に発表した戦略的協業の一環となるもの。

両社は東京・首都圏を中心に、リテール各社のメディア（サイネージ、アプリ広告、店内放送など）を横断活用することで、埋もれない情報伝達やリテールメディアのメディアパワーの実証・検証を行ってきた。

これまでのリテール横断でのPoC（概念実証）を通じて、横断的なリテールメディア活用の有効性が確認されたため、新団体の設立に至ったという。

従来の単体流通ごとの「販促費」ではなく、小売企業（売上高合計2.3兆円規模）横断のリテールメディアネットワークを構築することにより、「広告・マーケティングの在り方」を変革することを目指す。

研究会の発足に先立ち、2026年5月4日から5月31日まで、東京都、埼玉県、神奈川県、千葉県のスギ薬局、西友、トライアル計401店舗を対象に、サイネージおよび店内放送を横断して展開するPoCを実施した。

人流データを基に算出した4週間の重複除外後の推計ユニーク来店者数は約685万人となり、700万人規模の生活者へ接触できる可能性を確認した。

トライアルグループとスギ薬局の双方を利用した来店者は全体の約2.1％にとどまり、そのうちスギ薬局と西友の重複は約1.8％だった。

両グループの顧客層の重複が少ないことから、メディアを横断することで、リーチの重複を抑えながら接触可能な生活者を広げられると考えている。

今後、研究会では小売企業横断型リテールメディアネットワークの構築とその効果、「広告的価値」「販促的価値」両輪での効果検証方法の構築、TVCMにおけるGRP（グロスレーティングポイント）のようなリテールメディアにおける共通指標作りなどを進めていく。

domestic.title: 車内「あるある」あなたは大丈夫？阪急・阪神などでマナー啓発ポスターとデジタルサイネージ掲出
domestic.content:
【ニュースの要約】
日本民営鉄道協会による駅と電車内のマナー啓発ポスター・デジタルサイネージが、10月1日から11月30日まで、加盟72社の駅構内や列車内に掲出されます。兵庫県内では阪急電鉄、阪神電気鉄道、神戸電鉄、山陽電気鉄道などが対象です。

今回の啓発では、2025年12月に発表された「駅と電車内の迷惑行為ランキング（2025年度）」を参考に、電車内で見かける「イヤなあるある」をテーマとしたデザインを採用しています。

荷物の扱い方や咳エチケットなど、日常生活の中で無意識にしてしまいがちな行動をイラストで表現し、自身の振る舞いを振り返るきっかけとなる内容です。

ポスターは、駅貼り用のB1・B2サイズと中吊り用のB3サイズを用意。デジタルサイネージとあわせて、誰もが共感しやすい身近な場面を通して、周囲への配慮を伝えます。

掲出枚数は駅構内が約2,000枚、電車内が約23,000枚。全国の対象駅や列車で、期間中に一斉掲出されます。

同協会では、1997年から駅と電車内のマナー啓発ポスターを掲出しています。携帯電話の普及をきっかけに始まり、時勢に合わせて内容やデザインを見直しながら継続されています。

毎日の通勤やお出かけでたくさんの人が利用する電車だからこそ、気になる車内での振る舞い。身近な「あるある」をきっかけに、自分自身のマナーを見直す機会になりそうです。

domestic.title: 購買データでブランドは育つのか？ リテールメディア が抱える高額な検証コスト
domestic.content:
【ニュースの要約】
リテールメディアネットワーク（以下、RMN：Retail Media Network）が当初掲げていた提案は、買い物中の客を見つけ出し、購買へと結びつけることであった。

RMNがその目的を達成したいま、各社はそれぞれのチャネル上でブランドを構築できると広告主（そして彼らのさらなる広告予算）に納得させようと試みている。

Amazon以外のRMNも、提携で「フルファネル」の機能を揃える

独自のテクノロジースタック、効果測定能力、ストリーミングチャンネルを擁するリテールメディア界のマンモス企業である Amazon以外のすべての小売業者にとって、RMNはパートナーシップを通じてこの提供価値を強化してきた 。

つまり、自前のストリーミングプラットフォームやテクノロジースタックを持たない小売業者各社は、そうした機能を提供するために提携を結んできたのだ。

たとえば、クローガー（Kroger）とディズニー・アドバタイジング（Disney Advertising）の提携、ウォルマートとTikTok、メタ（Meta）、スナップ（Snap）との提携、あるいはインスタカート（Instacart）とエヌビーシーユニバーサル（NBCUniversal）との提携がそれに当たる。

トレード・スクール（Trade School）のリテールメディア担当エグゼクティブディレクターであるキム・メイヨ氏は、Digidayへの電子メール声明で「小売業者はオンラインの広告枠を遥かに超えるものを所有している。彼らは 商品棚、デジタルスクリーン、アプリ、コンテンツ、そして文化的な瞬間そのもの を掌握しているのだ」と語った。

RMNは購買直前のコンバージョン獲得だけでなく、ファーストパーティデータやオフサイト広告を活用したブランド構築へと領域を広げようとしている。

しかし多くのRMNは広告商品や測定手法が依然としてROASや購買獲得を重視しており、ブランド広告の成果を証明しにくいという課題を抱えている。

さらにブランド側でも予算の出どころが曖昧で、ブランド構築に必要な投資を確保しにくい。RMNのフルファネル化には広告商品と測定の変革が求められる。

domestic.title: トライアルHD・スギ薬局、リテールメディア研究会「TOKYO Retail Media Federation」を発足
domestic.source: ダイヤモンド・チェーンストアオンライン
domestic.content:
【ニュースの要約】
（画像）トライアルホールディングス・ニュースリリースより

トライアルホールディングス（福岡県）とスギ薬局（愛知県）は、両社が掲げる戦略的協業の一環として、小売企業横断のリテールメディアネットワークの構築、効果検証方法の確立、共通指標の策定を研究する「TOKYO Retail Media Federation（東京リテールメディア研究会）」を発足したと9月30日に発表した。

リテールメディアは、購買に近い場所で生活者へ情報を届け、広告接触と購買行動を結び付けて検証できるメディアとして活用が広がっている。一方、小売企業ごとに媒体、販売方法、効果指標が異なるため、複数の小売企業を横断した広告展開や効果比較には課題が残っている。

両社は東京・首都圏を中心に、リテール各社のメディア（サイネージ、アプリ広告、店内放送など）を横断活用することで、リテールメディアのメディアパワーの実証・検証を行ってきた。これまでのリテール横断でのPoC（概念実証）を通じて、横断的なリテールメディア活用の有効性が確認されたため、研究会の設立に至った。

従来の単体流通ごとの「販促費」ではなく、小売企業（2社の売上高合計2.3兆円規模）横断のリテールメディアネットワークを構築することにより、「広告・マーケティングの在り方」を変革することを目指す。

研究会の発足に先立ち、5月4日から5月31日まで、東京都、埼玉県、神奈川県、千葉県のスギ薬局、西友、トライアル計401店舗を対象に、サイネージおよび店内放送を横断して展開するPoCを実施した。

その結果、人流データを基に算出した4週間の重複除外後の推計ユニーク来店者数は約685万人となり、700万人規模の生活者へ接触できる可能性を確認した。また、両グループの顧客層の重複が少なく、メディアを横断することでリーチの重複を抑えながら接触可能な生活者を広げられることが示された。

domestic.title: 博報堂がリテールメディア7社と連携、認知から購買まで横断した統合メディアプラニングが可能に（Web担当者Forum）
domestic.content:
【ニュースの要約】
「Tele-Digi AaaS Simulator」に「イオンチャンネル」「ファミマTV」など追加

博報堂と博報堂テクノロジーズは、メディアプラニングソリューション「Tele-Digi AaaS Simulator」の対象媒体にリテールメディアを追加したと10月2日に発表した。主要リテールメディア提供企業7社と連携を強化した。従来のテレビ広告やデジタル広告、コネクテッドTV広告、屋外・交通広告(ODM)に加えて、複数企業の広範なリテールメディアを横断したリーチ効率や最適予算配分のシミュレーションできる。生活者の日常的なメディア接触から実際の店舗空間まで多様な接点を網羅し、精緻で統合的なメディアプラニングを実現する。

AaaS、7社のリテールメディア提供企業と連携   連携するのは(1)イオンリテール「イオンチャンネルAD」「イオンチャンネル」、 ウエルシア薬局「ウエルシア薬局サイネージ」(情報はMADS)、(3)ゲート・ワン「ファミマTV」(ファミリーマート店舗内サイネージ)、(4)セブン‐イレブン・ジャパン(セブン‐イレブンのデジタルサイネージ広告)、(5)ツルハホールディングス「ツルハグループサイネージ広告」「ツルハグループ横断エンドサイネージ広告」(情報はアドインテ)、(6)DearOne(NTTドコモグループ)「ARUTANA」、(7)パン・パシフィック・インターナショナルホールディングス(PPIH)「ドンドンTV」(五十音順)。  生活者のメディア接点や購買経路が複雑化し、認知から購買までのメディア施策効果の可視化とメディア投資の最適化が求められている。店頭サイネージとアプリ等のリテールメディアは生活動線上の新たな認知獲得・ブランド構築のメディアとして重要性を増しているため、博報堂と博報堂テクノロジーズは国内主要リテールメディア提供企業7社と大規模な連携を実現。各社の膨大かつ多様なメディアデータを適切に集約・分析して、特定の小売りチャネルに偏らずに生活者の幅広い購買行動を捉える独自のシミュレーションロジックを開発した。

フリーランス記者・編集者。「Web担当者Forum」でニュース記事を担当。「ASCII STARTUP」や「空港の裏方お仕事図鑑」などでも執筆。東洋経済新報社の会社四季報編集部の記者として上場企業を取材中。毎日新聞社で電機メーカーや情報通信、重工業、化学工業、化粧品・日用品業界のほか、東京証券取引所、総務省、経済産業省、国土交通省など霞ヶ関を取材。ニュースサイトの編集・編成業務の10年を経て2019年9月退社し独立。

global.title: Focus on India: Digital Signage Market Enters a New Growth Phase
global.titleEn: Focus on India: Digital Signage Market Enters a New Growth Phase
global.content:
【ニュースの要約】
Florian Rotberg and Stefan Schieker of invidis at Infocomm India (Image: Avixa)     While Europe and North America are increasingly characterized by replacement cycles and modernization projects, India remains largely a greenfield market. Digital signage adoption is still in its early stages across many verticals, creating significant room for expansion over the coming years.  A Billion-Dollar Market in the Making      According to the market outlook presented by invidis at the conference, the Indian digital signage market is expected to approach USD 1 billion in annual volume by 2026, representing roughly 20% of the total EMEA market opportunity.  Growth continues to outpace global averages by a wide margin. Annual expansion rates between 12% and 15% make India one of the fastest-growing digital signage markets worldwide, growing two to three times faster than many established regions.  Unlike mature markets where investment often focuses on replacing existing infrastructure, Indian projects are still predominantly greenfield deployments. New stores, office campuses, transportation hubs and public infrastructure projects create fresh demand rather than replacement demand, providing a strong foundation for sustainable growth.   India’s retail industry has evolved into one of the world’s most dynamic and fast-growing sectors, making a significant contribution to the country’s economic development.  According to  BCG and the Retailers Association of India , the Indian retail market is projected to reach an impressive USD 2 trillion by 2034, expanding at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 9%. Organised retail currently accounts for around 18% of the market, while the remaining 82% is made up of the vast unorganised sector, comprising millions of small independent shops.  In terms of store count, organised retail represents only a few hundred thousand outlets compared to an estimated 13-15 million unorganised stores. However, the organised segment is expanding rapidly, creating significant opportunities for digital signage and in-store media networks. At the same time, parts of the unorganised sector, particularly larger independent retailers, are beginning to experiment with entry-level signage solutions such as smartphones, tablets, and tabletop displays powered by simple media players.  India remains one of the fastest-growing retail markets globally and is on track to become the world’s third-largest retail market by 2030.        Digital Signage Conference at Infocomm India (Image: Avixa)       Digital Signage Conference at Infocomm India (Image: Avixa)       Digital Signage Conference at Infocomm India (Image: Avixa)       Digital Signage Conference at Infocomm India (Image: Avixa)       Florian Rotberg and Stefan Schieker of invidis at Infocomm India (Image: Avixa)    Four Key Drivers Shaping the Market  Industry experts identified four major growth engines behind India’s signage boom.  Organized retail continues to modernize rapidly as national and international brands expand across the country. Modern retail concepts increasingly rely on digital communication, customer engagement and real-time content management.  The second major driver is Digital-out-of-Home and in-store retail media. DooH is booming across India – primarily in large metropolitan areas but increasingly also in 2nd and 3rd tier cities. Retailers are beginning to recognize digital screens as revenue-generating assets rather than purely communication tools. The growing convergence of retail, data analytics and advertising is creating entirely new business models.  A third growth area is the deployment of large-scale LED installations. From landmark projects and corporate headquarters to transportation and public spaces, LED technology has become a highly visible symbol of India’s digital transformation.  Finally, ongoing smart city initiatives continue to generate demand for public information systems, wayfinding solutions and connected digital infrastructure across urban environments.     Experiences: Gulf Expertise for India’s Iconic Projects       Digital Signage Becomes Mission Critical  The conference also highlighted how signage strategies in India are evolving.  For many years, digital signage projects were isolated installations with limited connectivity and little business integration. Today, the market is rapidly moving toward fully connected ecosystems integrated into broader enterprise technology landscapes.  As a result, digital signage is increasingly shifting from a “nice-to-have” marketing tool to a business-critical platform. Organizations expect measurable outcomes, operational efficiencies and direct business impact.  The technology journey reflects this transformation: many networks have progressed from simple USB-stick content distribution to cloud-connected platforms and increasingly integrated experiences that connect signage with data, retail systems and customer engagement tools.  Equally important is a mindset shift among end users. Digital signage is no longer viewed solely as a cost center but increasingly as a profit lever, especially in retail media environments where screens directly contribute to advertising revenues and sales performance.  Make in India Creates New Opportunities  India’s rapidly expanding electronics manufacturing sector was another central topic of discussion.  Driven by the government’s “Make in India” initiative and global supply chain diversification, significant manufacturing capacity for display and LED technologies is being built across the country. Companies such as LED display specialist LedX are examples of a growing domestic production ecosystem.  Industry participants also noted increasingly pragmatic trade relations between India and China, helping stabilize component sourcing and manufacturing operations.  At the same time, India is positioning itself as an export hub. A potential future free trade agreement between India and the European Union could further improve market access for Indian-made hardware, software and services, creating new opportunities for global signage vendors and integrators.     Infocomm India: Global Brands Discover India       India’s Software Ecosystem Comes of Age  The conference also provided valuable insights into India’s software landscape.  While Samsung and LG proprietary CMS platforms still represent the largest installed software base across the country, a growing number of domestic vendors have established strong market positions. Key players include Jio Signage, Pickcel, Wilyer, Xtreme Media and Zeetaminds.  Beyond the domestic market, India has become one of the world’s most important software development centers for the digital signage industry. Many global independent software vendors (ISVs) rely on Indian development teams to build and maintain products deployed worldwide.  Interestingly, several Indian software providers have achieved greater commercial success internationally than within their home market. Low domestic software pricing, where average license fees often remain in the single-digit euro range, continues to create challenges for premium software providers.  At the same time, weakening demand in some Middle Eastern markets has encouraged many Indian software companies to place greater emphasis on opportunities within the rapidly growing domestic market.  India Moves to the Center of the Global Signage Industry  The key message from the Invidis Digital Signage Conference at InfoComm India was clear: India is no longer an emerging side market. It is becoming one of the industry’s most important growth engines.  A unique combination of economic growth, retail modernization, smart city investments, manufacturing expansion and software expertise is creating momentum across the entire digital signage value chain. As global vendors and service providers increasingly look beyond mature markets for growth, India is moving from a market of future potential to a market of present opportunity. The launch extends retail media beyond traditional grocery environments into high-frequency convenience, where suppliers can connect with shoppers in impulse-led moments.

7-Eleven Australia has more than 760 stores and registers 4.6 million weekly transactions, making it one of the largest convenience retailers in the country.

A new in-store digital screen network rollout has commenced and will expand further in 2027, increasing opportunities for high-impact in-store engagement.

Anytime Media will be led by Anthony Venuto, the GM of commercial services at 7-Eleven Australia.

“7-Eleven has millions of weekly customer interactions, the strongest product launch and recruitment offer in the market and a thriving loyalty platform. It’s on this strong platform that Anytime Media @ 7-Eleven will boost advertiser campaigns and better connect with target audiences,” he said.

Riley Wolff, the product manager of Anytime Media @ 7-Eleven, added: “We’ve built Anytime Media @ 7-Eleven to help brand partners better engage young Australians, elevate innovation and create more meaningful moments in and out of store. The network, including our new digital screen rollout, is designed to help supplier advertisers maximise impact, create value and activate in moments that matter.”

Recently,  Commonwealth Bank ,  Virgin Australia ,  Bunnings ,  David Jones  and  Metcash  have set up commerce networks.

Meanwhile  McDonald’s has begun a US trial  of its commerce media network.

global.title: Kroger takes key step forward in tying retail media creative with digital sales
global.titleEn: Kroger takes key step forward in tying retail media creative with digital sales
global.content:
【ニュースの要約】
The grocer, in partnership with Vidmob and MMA Global, was able to forecast e-commerce conversion of ad creative with 81% accuracy.

Kroger has found that it can forecast e-commerce purchase conversion by using predictive creative scoring before campaigns are launched.

This audio is auto-generated. Please let us know if you have  feedback .

Kroger, in partnership with data firm Vidmob and trade association MMA Global, has found that it can forecast e-commerce purchase conversion by using predictive creative scoring before campaigns are launched and media is activated, per a study shared with sister publication Marketing Dive. The study brought together Kroger’s live campaign data, Vidmob’s creative data platform and MMA Global’s industry research standards to evaluate creative across variables including messaging, narrative structure, branding and on-screen human interaction.

The results find a strong tie between creative decisions and business outcomes, with predictive creative scoring able to forecast e-commerce conversion with 81% accuracy. Creative aligned with recommendations generated an average four-times improvement in conversion rates, and reallocating media toward higher-scoring media can potentially generate more than twice as many conversions from the same ad budget.

“[There are] two types of creative optimization. One is actually making changes, moving pixels around, changing the nature of the creative. But the other is just like moving dollars behind better creative,” said Alex Collmer, founder and executive chairman at Vidmob.

Kroger’s test of predictive creative scoring follows a  similar effort by Kellanova  — also with Vidmob and MMA Global — that connected creative decision with view-through rates, which the CPG marketer used as a proxy for sales. The new study forgoes proxies and demonstrates the connection to actual sales, providing a framework that could change how marketers optimize campaigns.

“Historically, people made [ads] and then, effectively, spent money blindly behind them, and then after the fact, looked to make optimizations once they saw performance,” Collmer said. “The ability to get ahead of that and basically not spend behind assets that aren’t going to work is a pretty big deal.”

The study used artificial intelligence to analyze more than 1,900 video and image assets from Kroger campaigns across Meta and Google’s DV360 and identified creative attributes that are tied to e-commerce conversion. The work continues Vidmob’s efforts to prove that creative quality is measurable, which in turn makes investment in creative more practical.

“For too long, the industry has existed in this world where creative investments are labeled non-working and media investments are working. That’s just absurd,” Collmer said. “Every marketer you talk to says creative is 50% to 70% of results. How on earth can the thing that’s the far majority of results be the waste?”

global.title: GSTV: What’s Next For Retail Media in Convenience
global.titleEn: GSTV: What’s Next For Retail Media in Convenience
global.content:
【ニュースの要約】
NACS Media recently caught up with GSTV CEO Eric Kozik to discuss opportunities retailers should be watching.

As retailers look for new ways to engage customers and drive growth, retail media continues to gain momentum across the convenience channel. NACS Media recently caught up with GSTV CEO Eric Kozik to discuss industry trends, evolving consumer behavior and opportunities retailers should be watching.   What are the biggest initiatives GSTV is focused on right now?   Everything we're working on comes back to one question: how do we create more value from the forecourt for our retail partners?  First, growing our network with those partners. We continue to add sites with retailers across the country, and we're working with our hardware partners to bring new screen technology and a more seamless network and content experience into the field. We’re planning to announce additional exciting new partnerships and are grateful for the retailers and industry leaders who are growing their business with GSTV as their trusted media partner.  Second, bringing more demand to the screens retailers already have. We've upgraded the technology across our entire network and added new programmatic partnerships, which makes it easier for CPG brands to engage with customers as they fuel and share targeted and relevant messaging that drive sales.  Third, we’re offering retailers more ways to partner together. From managed service models to being easier than ever to get GSTV up and running on the forecourt, we want to be that “easy button” for retailers to have media drive consumers from the forecourt and into stores.   What excites you most as you look ahead to the next few months?    As we wrap up 2026 and head into 2027, what excites me is that the industry is starting to recognize the value of the attentive moments they have with consumers in their forecourts and are eager to leverage media more than ever before. The fuel and convenience channel is where a lot of purchase journeys begin, but all too often it starts and ends with a fuel purchase only. Our job is to make sure the journey includes a short walk inside the store with a purchase already in mind.  The best retailers understand that relevance matters as much as reach. They know why a customer is stopping, whether it's a morning coffee, a lunch run or a road trip, and they build the experience around that mission, starting the moment the car pulls in.   What notable developments are you seeing among convenience retailers today?   Convenience stores are becoming destinations. Shoppers are coming in for fresh food, new products and emerging brands, and they're building those visits into their daily routines. Furthermore, those routines show up in a retailer’s data.  That's a big opportunity for retailers, and it changes the job. When people arrive with a reason to come inside, the question becomes ‘how early you can shape what they buy?’ For most shoppers, that starts at the pump, before they ever walk through the door. That's the moment GSTV helps retailers make the most of and optimize both the consumer behavior and the data.   Based on GSTV's recent consumer behavior research, what did you find most surprising about consumers today?   What stands out is how intentional these stops at the c-store have become, and how many of the season's biggest moments run through our retail partners' stores. In our latest Consumer Pulse research,  80% of GSTV viewers said they're planning or considering a road trip this fall , and 73% of road trippers stop at gas stations and convenience stores for snacks or breaks along the way.  Another number that our recent Pulse study uncovered is this one: 96% of viewers who saw an ad at the gas station went on to recognize the brand, consider it, research it or buy it. That's a shopper who is still deciding, standing a few feet from your front door. Research like this is part of what we bring to our retail partners, so they can plan around the moments that bring shoppers in.   What retail media opportunities do you think convenience retailers are still overlooking?   The forecourt itself. Too often, retail media in our channel is thought of as happening on an app or a shelf. But the bigger question underneath all of it is where the shopping decision actually starts. For a lot of customers, it starts at the pump, before they ever walk inside.  The forecourt is one of the few places in retail media where the retailer owns both the audience and the moment. Retailers who treat it as valuable media, not just a place to fuel up, will unlock value many are leaving on the table today.   What's one opportunity that you think the industry is underestimating right now?   How much younger shoppers rely on convenience stores, and how much they enjoy them. Our research this year found that 76% of GSTV's Gen Z viewers visit a convenience store at least once a week, and they're 17% more likely than our average viewer to go inside after fueling up. Nearly all of them (97%) say they enjoy browsing the store, and they're 31% more likely than any other generation to discover new products there.  Gen Z tunes out ads almost everywhere else, but according to our research gas station video ranks first with them across channels, so the forecourt is one of the best places a retailer has to reach them. Retailers who catch these shoppers at the pump, then give them something worth discovering inside, will earn a customer who keeps coming back.   As retailers prepare for the future, what should they be paying more attention to heading into 2027?   Outcomes. Brands are under more pressure than ever to prove their media works, and they're moving budget to the places that can show it.  That's where retailers hold the key. A media partner can show that a message reached a shopper at the pump, but knowing what happened inside a specific store takes the retailer's data. The retailers willing to share that data with their partners will be able to show brands exactly what their forecourt delivers, and they'll capture more of that spend in 2027.  It also changes how retailers should think about the forecourt. The screen at the pump is the hook: it's the first time a shopper hears from you on that visit. The retailers getting the most out of it connect that first message to what comes next: the offer inside the store, the loyalty app, the promotion at the register. That way the whole visit tells one story.  Retail media is moving off the screens in people's hands and into the real world, closer to the moment someone decides to buy. The fuel and convenience channel is where that happens every day, and our retail partners are at the center of it.

Noelle Riddle is an Editor/Writer at NACS.
