global.content:
【ニュースの要約】
The integration enables media players running on the Hub AV (formerly Tripleplay) platform toautomatically identify themselves to Extreme Fabric Attach, enabling network administrators to apply preconfigured policies and automate device provisioning, eliminating the need formanual, device-by-device network configuration.

New integration with Extreme Fabric streamlines media player provisioning across sports venues, enterprises and other connected environments..  Image: Uniguest

The collaboration is particularly relevant for stadiums, arenas and large venues, where reliable delivery of live video, digital signage and venue information across hundreds or thousands of screens is essential. It complements Uniguest's Sports Hub solution, while also supporting Enterprise Hub and applications across hospitality, education and other connected environments.

This partnership is particularly relevant for large venues such as stadiums and arenas.  Image: Uniguest

Beyond simplified provisioning, the collaboration also validates Hub AV’s IPTV and digital signage capabilities across Extreme Networks infrastructure for customers using Extreme Fabric, including high-availability failover, reliable multicast IPTV delivery, and frame-synchronised media playback across multiple displays.

Pankaj Kulkarni, EVP of Product Management at Uniguest, commented: “Sports venues and enterprises need technology that's not only powerful and reliable, but also straightforward to deploy and manage. By integrating with Extreme Fabric Attach, we're making it easier for customers to deploy IPTV and digital signage across their networks, while reducing the time and complexity involved in configuring individual devices. Combined with the breadth of our platform, this gives organisations a flexible, scalable solution for managing content across their facilities.”

“An arena may host basketball one night and a sold-out concert the next, with different demands for signage, live video and sponsor content,” said Chuck Brooks, Director of Ecosystems and Alliances at Extreme Networks. “By automating how supported Uniguest media players connect to Extreme Fabric, we help venue teams add or relocate screens with less manual network configuration. That means less time configuring connections and more time creating experiences that engage fans and deliver value for sponsors.” (stadiaworld, 05.11.2026)

global.title: Retail media is a $200bn market with a blind spot outside the store. A Swiss technology company has built the answer.
global.titleEn: Retail media is a $200bn market with a blind spot outside the store. A Swiss technology company has built the answer.
global.content:
【ニュースの要約】
There were 2,552 press releases posted in the last 24 hours and 504,185 in the last 365 days.

November 05, 2026, 12:38 GMT

Invenda's Atlas platform turns the screens of smart vending machines into advertising space at the POS. The ad and the sale happen on the same device.

Unlike street-side DOOH screens, Invenda smart vending machines are points of sale. They stand where people pause, choose and buy, not just pass by, and they hold attention through longer dwell times and interaction with the machine. With Atlas, each screen becomes a media channel with its own conversion path: the product sits behind the display that advertises it, and ad plays and purchases are logged on the same machine, so a campaign can be matched to the sales it drives.

Brands can choose between two formats on the interactive screen: full-screen ads for launches and awareness campaigns, and a persistent top banner that stays visible while shoppers browse and buy. Where audience measurement is installed, anonymous insights show how many people saw an ad, for how long and in which context, with reporting built for agency campaign reviews.

Campaigns can be booked programmatically through leading demand-side platforms (DSPs) or directly with Invenda's media specialists, so agencies can keep their existing workflows. Atlas also supports interactive formats: shoppers can scan a code on the screen and win a product instantly from the machine, turning an ad into an action at the point of sale.

Invenda has a base of more than 7,500 smart screens in 22 countries, in environments such as travel hubs and hotels, fitness and wellness, retail, leisure and sports, offices, campuses and healthcare. For machine operators and location owners, Atlas adds a second revenue stream from the same screen. Brands and agencies can book campaigns, and operators and venues can add their locations to the network, at  www.invendagroup.com/advertise-dooh-network .

Invenda Group AG is a Swiss software company and the leader in Global Smart Vending, transforming automated retail and digital out-of-home (DOOH) advertising through its proprietary AI-powered platform. Invenda's technology connects and automates networks of smart vending machines, micro markets, and digital screens—enabling operators and brands to optimize operations, access real-time data, and unlock new revenue streams through location-based e-commerce and targeted advertising.

Headquartered in Alpnach, Switzerland, Invenda has locations in Berlin, New York, Miami, Hong Kong, Sofia, Zagreb, and Novi Sad. The company supports deployments in 22 countries and partners with global brands, operators, and manufacturers, including Mars Wrigley, Coca-Cola, Selecta, and Valora. Willem Allroggen

global.titleEn: OXXO rebrands its retail media platform as OXXO Media
global.content:
【ニュースの要約】
Published on: Nov 5, 2026

The former Retina Media combines in-store screens, direct messaging, the Spin Premia app and off-site campaigns, reaching around 13 million daily customers across nearly 25,000 stores in Mexico.

OXXO has renamed its retail media platform, Retina Media, as OXXO Media, building on the brand’s recognition among consumer goods manufacturers and media agencies. The platform combines technology, data, targeting and measurement across nearly 25,000 stores in Mexico, which serve around 13 million customers every day.  OXXO Media is built on four pillars. In stores, it offers advertising across the physical infrastructure and a network of digital screens that will reach almost 7,000 locations by the end of 2026. Its direct-to-consumer channel reaches shoppers through email, RCS, push notifications, SMS and WhatsApp.  On OXXO’s own platforms, brands can advertise on its website and the Spin Premia loyalty app, which has more than 29 million users. Off-site, campaigns run on Meta, Google and delivery apps, supported by OXXO’s first-party data.  FEMSA cites eMarketer data showing that around 89% of consumer goods purchases in the region still take place in physical stores. According to Trinity McQueen and Co-op Media Network, 68% of people walk into a convenience store without a shopping list.  “Behind every OXXO store there are people who, through their daily work, make the experience of millions of consumers possible,” said Juan Restrepo, Director of OXXO Media.

global.title: After DoorDash's Instacart bid, here's the case for and against consolidation in commerce media
global.titleEn: After DoorDash's Instacart bid, here's the case for and against consolidation in commerce media
global.content:
【ニュースの要約】
Join us Dec. 1-3 in Nashville for the Digiday Programmatic Marketing Summit

By  Kimeko McCoy    •   November 5, 2026   •

The “C” word (consolidation) might soon be coming for commerce media.

At least that was how media buyers and industry analysts reacted to last week’s news about DoorDash’s plans to acquire Instacart.

“We’ve seen this play out before in search, social, and streaming. Markets tend to consolidate around a few major players, and commerce media is heading in the same direction,” said Bill Wise, CEO and co-founder of Mediaocean, an ad tech company.

Should the deal, which is valued at approximately $17 billion, go through, it pairs DoorDash’s delivery network of 993 million total orders,  per DoorDash’s Q3 earnings  and Instacart’s grocery and fulfillment technology (as well as its 91.4 million orders,  per Instacart’s Q3 earnings ).

Retail Media Rewritten  		 Here are the questions on advertisers’ minds after the DoorDash-Instacart deal

Perhaps the biggest case in favor of consolidation in commerce media is that the playbook already exists in ad tech. For example, Gopuff announced plans in September to leverage Instacart’s white-label retail media platform Carrot Ads. Both Gopuff and Instacart have separate commerce media networks.

“You could kind of argue data consolidation is also happening across partners who are working together to make their joint offerings more compelling,” said Briana Finelli, vp of brand and commerce media at Goodway Group.

As for the DoorDash-Instacart deal specifically, the upsides are a broader audience, more powerful closed-loop reporting capabilities, combined tech offerings and a more simplified media buying experience (buying with a single combined platform as opposed to across two individuals).

domestic.title: シルバーアイが店舗の販促・広告運用を支えるデジタルサイネージ配信CMS「SIGNAGEi 2.0」をリリース
domestic.content:
【ニュースの要約】
シルバーアイは、65,000面以上の導入実績を持つSIGNAGEiシリーズで培った知見を生かし、CMSのサービス提供に加えて、ディスプレイや配信端末の選定、施工、コンテンツ制作、配信・運用、監視・保守まで一貫してサポート。小売・飲食などの多店舗事業者が、継続して活用できる店舗メディアづくりに取り組みます。

近年、不正アクセスやサイバー攻撃による情報漏えい、システムの停止などが社会的な課題となり、企業には事業の継続と信頼を守るためのセキュリティ対策が求められています。

ネットワークを通じて情報を配信するデジタルサイネージにおいても、管理画面への不正アクセスやアカウントの不適切な利用は、配信内容の改ざんや意図しない情報の表示、運用停止などにつながるおそれがあります。店舗やブランドの情報を生活者に届ける仕組みとして、CMSの機能面と、その利用・管理体制の両面で対策を講じることが重要です。

こうした背景を踏まえ、SIGNAGEi 2.0は、アカウント管理やアクセス制御などのセキュリティ対応と、AI・天気・POSデータを活用した情報発信を支援します。シルバーアイは、導入から配信運営・保守までの知見を生かし、お客様が店舗メディアを安心して継続的に活用できる環境づくりに取り組みます。

本部や店舗など、複数の担当者が関わるサイネージ運用を想定し、アカウント管理やアクセス制御を通じて、適切な利用環境づくりを支援します。あわせて、配信前の承認や操作の記録により、誤配信の防止を支援します。多要素認証により、ID・パスワードだけに依存しない認証に対応します。

また、オンプレミス環境での導入についてもご相談いただけます。お客様のネットワーク環境や社内規程、管理体制を確認し、要件に応じた導入構成を検討します。

2. AIレコメンドによる情報発信の企画・運用支援

AIレコメンド機能を活用し、情報発信の企画・運用における判断を支援します。AIが店舗の客層や時間帯、過去の配信実績をもとに、理由を示して配信内容を提案します。

担当者は提案を参考に配信内容を判断し、店舗や目的に応じた情報発信に活用できます。

3. 天気・POSデータを活用した、店舗に合わせた情報発信

global.title: Criteo To Handle Adore Beauty’s Retail Media Business
global.titleEn: Criteo To Handle Adore Beauty’s Retail Media Business
global.content:
【ニュースの要約】
Criteo, a commerce media adtech platform, has inked a new retail media partnership with Adore Beauty, an Australian online beauty retailer.

The partnership will see Criteo power its retail media offering across Australia and New Zealand.

Through this deal, Adore Beauty will introduce onsite Sponsored Products advertising across its digital environments, powered by Criteo’s retail media technology. The offering will enable brand partners to reach Adore Beauty customers at key moments of product discovery, consideration and purchase.

The initial launch will see sponsored products introduced across Adore Beauty’s search and category pages, beginning on web before extending to the app.

A second phase is expected to explore product detail page and onsite display ads, creating additional opportunities for beauty brands to connect with shoppers throughout the purchase journey.

Criteo will support the integration, advertiser demand, campaign activation, reporting and closed loop measurement through its Commerce Yield and Commerce Max platforms.

The partnership builds on Criteo’s existing relationship with Adore Beauty, where Criteo supports customer acquisition and measurable growth through performance campaigns. Adore Beauty’s data-driven attribution enables the retailer to evaluate Criteo’s contribution across the broader customer journey, rather than relying solely on last click measurement.

“Our customers come to Adore Beauty to discover, explore and shop from a wide range of beauty brands, so there is a natural opportunity to bring brands closer to customers throughout that experience,” said Katrina Rose, chief digital officer, Adore Beauty.

“Working with Criteo will allow us to build out our retail media offering and give our brand partners new ways to connect with customers at relevant moments in their shopping journey.”

The retail media partnership extends this collaboration onto Adore Beauty’s own digital properties, bringing together Criteo’s expertise in performance optimisation, audience activation and attribution with Adore Beauty’s first-party data and high intent shopping environment.
